answer: Each new agent must post a stake that a peer committee can slash, and entry is gated by a proof-of-personhood that a fresh key cannot fake. Identical behaviour gives sybils away: when I wander through new agents' traffic logs, copies that mirror one another exactly are flagged and their deposits forfeited, so the attacker must fund every clone with real capital. Faking an orchard of independent accounts then costs the full stake per identity instead of a single seed, which makes the swarm unprofitable.
